doc.title: Mike Vax interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, December 29, 2022

title: Keeping the band on the road in 1971 and discipline
summary: When Kenton was ill in 1971 Vax fought for payment, including at the Loser's Club in Dallas, and handled discipline and notice.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Getting paid: wages, scale and the pay envelope

blocks.x: be able to re-join the band but the doctors want him to stay a little longer. Well it was all lies because you know we had to keep the band on the road for him. So I had to pretend that, oh gee I really did think Stan was going to be joining us but they just said at the last minute he can’t. So then they would, a lot of times, especially clubs and things like that, they’d try to say well you broke the contract because Stan isn’t here. And I’d say, “You sold out, we’re trying to keep this band on the road for Stan while he’s sick and you’re sold out. You made money, don’t give me that stuff about you know we broke the contract and you want to — a couple of places you know they’d given the 50% deposit and they wanted to not pay the other 50%. And I had to fight with them and all except one club, The Loser’s Club — believe it or not it was The Loser’s Club in Dallas, and that was a huge scene where the guy, you know he had sort of like his own little Mafia thing and he had these guys with guns and all that. So we’re back there and Dick Shearer and I are trying to say, “You know come on, you sold out, we were here two nights, you sold out.” Willie Maiden brings some of the bigger guys back in there and the guy’s got his two thugs and Willie says, “Listen man, if this is going to be like back in the 30s, man, if you don’t pay the band we’re going to wreck the club.”
I think Willie Maiden would have had to bring some of the bigger guys ‘cause he looked like —

Oh yeah exactly. And that was the only place in the five months that Stan was gone that I didn’t get the rest of the money. All the rest you know it was part of what my job was. Yeah as road manager there were times that I had to do some disciplining, especially when Stan was gone. Because when the cat’s away the mice will play so to speak. And it’s not like the guys were taking advantage but again, they were getting complacent a little bit and taking advantage. And there were a couple of times where I had to threaten to fire guys. I didn’t actually fire anybody while Stan was gone. I had to fire some people other times where Stan, you know that was one of my duties. Stan said get rid of them. But I didn’t have to fire anybody while Stan was gone. Everybody believed we have to keep this band on the road for Stan because we love him.
Was there a union rule of a sort that you had to give like a two week notice either way — if a guy wanted to quit, two weeks, etcetera.

Yeah, exactly. And that’s only fair both sides. So that’s what we would do. Or if there was some instance, there was only one instance I can remember where it was just a situation where the guy needed to be gone and Stan basically paid him his two weeks and sent him home and got somebody else.
